issue.title: Obsidian Bases cells edit record frontmatter raw, bypassing bob validation and leaving the [!records] index stale
issue.description: Obsidian Bases views (e.g. sase_blog_zettel.base) let a cell edit write a record's frontmatter key directly. That path is schema-blind: it can store a non-choice value (Ready instead of ready), skips required/bounds/URL checks, never rebuilds the parent album's [!records] callout (stale until the next bob albums sync), and re-serializes the whole frontmatter block, the hazard bob-plugins already avoids by forbidding processFrontMatter. The planned Record Card makes concurrent Bases edits safe for its own writes via an expect fingerprint (a stale save refuses), but the Bases edit itself still lands invalid values and a stale index. Remediation is a design choice, e.g. lint surfacing via bob records check on vault change, a reconcile pass, or retiring Bases cell editing for record folders.

task_type_fields.impact: Any Bases cell edit can silently create an invalid record and a stale album index; the upcoming record sheet/card hides native Properties, making the stale/invalid state less visible unless the sheet lints it.
task_type_fields.location: Obsidian Bases files over record folders (e.g. sase_blog_zettel.base); contrast src/native/records/{plan,check}.rs validation and the [!records] rebuild in bob records update
task_type_fields.repro: Open an album's .base view in Obsidian, edit a choices cell (e.g. status) to an arbitrary string, then run bob records check -f json (reports record_invalid_value) and compare the album note's [!records] callout, which still shows the old grouping until bob albums sync.

issue.creation_reason: Found during the record-card research consolidation (research:202611/record_card/record_card__final.md): every researcher's design assumes bob is the only record writer, but Bases remains an unguarded second writer today.
